thread.title: TransCanada Is A True Dividend Growth Stock - TransCanada Corporation (NYSE:TRP)

author: Scott Wilkie
title: TransCanada Is A True Dividend Growth Stock - TransCanada Corporation (NYSE:TRP)
text:
We have been very fortunate to experience the growth in our markets that we have seen since the financial crisis of 2007-2008. During that period, many investors have watched their portfolios soar as the economy has grown at an extraordinary pace. But like any bull market, eventually all good things come to an end, and the cracks have already started to form. Government stimulus has started to be removed, interest rates are starting to normalize and US-led trade wars are feeding uncertainty into world economies. It’s during these times of uncertainty that we have to really evaluate the companies we are partnered with to ensure that our personal needs can continue to be met. As an early retiree that depends on my dividend income to pay the bills and fund my lifestyle, I look to companies like TransCanada Corp. ( TRP ) to help me sleep at night.
It’s really about the Income The incredible success of the stock market has been driven by strength across all sectors, but none more so than the tech stocks. Companies like Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG ) have led the way with incredible stock appreciation, but the problem with these companies is that because they pay little or no dividend, you have to rely on your ability to time the market and sell your positions to create a steady income. For a retiree like myself, I prefer a less complicated approach: I like my companies to pay me, I like dividends, I like dividends that grow.
With TransCanada, I get that steady income. Every three months, I can depend on that dividend check to show up in my bank account. With a current yield of 5.25%, I know that my money is working for me and regardless of some self-serving tweet I will still get paid.
The other thing that I like about dividends is that they take the emotion out of investing. Dividends tend to be a more accurate reflection of how a well-run and profitable company is doing, and companies with a long history of steady dividend growth are what I choose to build my portfolio around.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation )
In the case of TransCanada, it has managed to grow its dividend every year for the past 18 years. That means that in 2007 and 2008, when many companies were either holding or shrinking their dividends, TRP continued to grow its own. I believe that the same will hold true during the next market correction as well, and the reason is that the company's business is not tied directly to the health of the economy. People need to heat their homes, turn on the lights and drive their cars - a dispute with China is not going to change this.
Diversification is a key part of its success Diversification is a critical component in a rapidly changing world. Since 2000, TRP has invested more than $85 billion to grow its business. From being primarily a Canadian natural gas infrastructure company 20 years ago moving product from Western Canada to eastern markets and with smaller interests in US natural gas pipelines and Canadian energy, TRP has grown these businesses, including additional interests in liquids pipelines and a growing presence in Mexico. Today, it is a leading North American Energy infrastructure company and is continuing to grow.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
This diversification is very important, because not only does it secure stable revenues for today, but it also ensures that the company is well-positioned to take advantage of future growth opportunities as well. Despite the efforts of narrow-minded politicians who choose to believe that environmental protections are bad, the reality is that change is inevitable - and in energy, that means the adoption of more green energy and more environmentally friendly carbon fuels, in particular, natural gas.
Recognizing that coal-fired electricity generation is harmful to our environment, there has been a push to convert many of these older stations to natural gas, which is equally cost-effective and more environmentally friendly. With abundant supply in both Western Canada and the Eastern US, TRP has the infrastructure in place to meet this added demand and is planning future growth projects around it. The company has also invested in this growing trend in Mexico, as well building out natural gas pipelines that will feed its growing electrical generation needs.
There is also tremendous growth opportunity in Liquid Natural Gas, as evidenced by the recent approval of the $6.2 billion Coastal Gaslink project which will move gas from Western Canada to the BC coast. This project will allow export of LNG to Asian markets, where similar demand exists to power their growing need for electrical generation.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
All this opportunity surrounding natural gas does not mean there will be a marked decline in the demand for liquids either. Although the push is on to identify cleaner burning fuels and adopt electric power, the truth is that the need for oil continues to grow. Based on current estimates, the demand for oil will continue to grow at least through 2030 as the primary fuel for transportation and chemical production.
With continued uncertainty surrounding supply from Middle Eastern and other OPEC countries, it is understandable that major refiners and governments recognize the need to be energy independent. With one of the largest oil reserves in the world located in the Canadian Oil sands, the question becomes how do you move that product to market. Although efforts to build the Keystone XL pipeline continue to receive pushback, at some point there has to be a recognition that the oil will be extracted and that pipelines are the safest and most cost-effective way to move it. This recognition will continue to grow as more and more product is moved by rail - a much more expensive and dangerous form of transportation running through major population corridors. It is my expectation that Keystone XL will succeed in the courts and begin construction in 2019 or 2020.
Regardless of what happens with KXL, I believe that as investors, we have to be able to look past the smoke and recognize that TransCanada has sufficient projects in development to continue to drive the company forward and KXL should be treated as a bonus.
If you want to go somewhere, you need a good map Being a profitable company in a low-risk, highly regulated and contracted business is great, but future dividend growth will depend on being able to grow the business beyond the simple cost of living increases built into most contracts. So, getting from where we are to where we want to go requires a good map.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
For TRP, that map is easy to read. With a current market cap of around $100 billion, between now and 2023 TRP has $36 billion in secured capital projects that are being built and will add significantly to future revenues and profitability. This includes more than $10 billion in projects that will be entering into service in the next several months. These projects do not include KXL, reinforcing my previous comment that it should be looked at as a bonus but not a necessary building block for TRP to be successful.
With this in mind, it is easy to look at TransCanada’s dividend growth forecast and have confidence that it will be able to deliver. Presently, TransCanada is forecasting dividend increases of between 8% and 10% between 2019 and 2021. That should be comforting to a retiree who sees a market that is currently struggling to maintain its momentum and shows early signs of a correction that could significantly erode valuations. That is why I enjoy dividend investing - when the markets are up, I feel good watching the value of my portfolio grow, but when the markets correct, I continue to receive my income, and if I so choose, I can reinvest those dividends to supercharge my portfolio and grow dividends even quicker.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
Also offering comfort is that with a clear road map, it is easy for me to see that earning per share will continue to grow, and FFO will also continue to grow, further supporting future dividend increases beyond 2021.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
Dividend growth is supported by earnings, not promises Based on the first 3 quarters, we can see that TRP is on track towards meeting its forecast 8-10% dividend increase for 2019. Comparable earnings per common share were up 24%, comparable EBITDA was up 12% and comparable FFO was up 11%. Although the background noise surrounding pipelines seems to keep pressure on stock prices, the reality is that the company is doing well, and the fact that demand for its services is exceeding supply should continue to drive profitability. Add to this that with its dividend, currently sitting at 5.25%, it is at an attractive entry point.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
With a current payout ratio of 72.88%, TRP's dividend is manageable and provides the best payout coverage of the major pipeline companies. Factor in these new projects coming on-line by the early part of 2019 and there is support for the next increase.
Also important is an improving debt situation as the company continues to deleverage its balance sheet. This, combined with increasing earnings per share, should also provide additional support for future dividend increases.
A long runway of future growth opportunities Currently, the company's existing framework of natural gas pipelines supplies 25% of North America's demand, tapping into some of the most productive areas located in Western Canada and the Appalachian region. From this platform, it is able to supply population centers across Canada and the eastern US, with growth opportunities including LNG and contributions to growing Mexican infrastructure.
In liquids, TRP currently moves 20% of Canadian oil sands output through its Keystone pipeline and would more than double its output to the US Gulf Coast should the Keystone XL pipeline receive final approvals. This approval is of tremendous importance to Canada and would go a long way towards ensuring energy independence.
In Ontario, TransCanada currently supplies 30% of the province's electricity needs through Bruce Power, and with planned refurbishments, will secure that business for decades to come. This source of clean nuclear energy aligns with Canada’s commitments to reduce greenhouse gases, while providing a dependable base load of electricity for the country’s largest province.
(Source: TransCanada Investor Presentation)
Of course, there are always concerns During these times of heightened environmental awareness, challenges are always present in running a $100 billion infrastructure company. Challenges to KXL continue to elevate costs and create uncertainty, but it will not impact revenues until beyond 2021 and is not factored into current forecasts. Regarding the completion of its Mexico projects, there are challenges related to corrupt practices concerning permits, not typically encountered by the company, but needing to be remedied before the projects continue. These issues and others like them will continue to create news, but should not overshadow the financial health of TransCanada and its future prospects.
As a retiree, it is really all about the income As an early retiree without a company or government pension to fall back on, I recognize that enjoying a lifestyle really comes down to income. At 53, I am fortunate to have achieved financial independence living on dividends generated by the companies I have partnered with through the years.
When I built my portfolio, I did so with the idea that the companies I owned should be able to survive the ups and downs of the markets. I am not one who likes to swing for the fences all the time, but feel comfortable hitting singles and doubles, knowing that these efforts will come around to score. Likewise, with TransCanada, I am happy to see my income going up at an 8-10% pace, knowing that the company is supported by a strong foundation that continues to grow and continues to provide for me and my family while I sleep well at night.
Disclosure: I am/we are long TRP.
